alt: Poster: SEBI eases margin rule after early pay-in - circular dated 22 Oct 2026, effective within four months, cash segment net sellers
text:
SEBI has eased margin requirements for clients who sell shares and use early pay-in, and the market is discussing it.

• SEBI's circular dated 22 October 2026 says clearing corporations will not collect margin on a client's subsequent buy or sell positions in the cash segment, up to the value of securities for which an early pay-in (EPI) request has been accepted, per Business Today and LiveLaw.
• The client must have a net sell obligation in a settlement; the available EPI value is the lower of the EPI value completed and the value of securities sold, per Business Today and LiveLaw.
• If the client squares off the sale position tied to the EPI benefit, the EPI value is removed and any resulting margin shortfall is blocked from the member's proprietary collateral, per Business Today and LiveLaw.
• The framework does not apply to trade-for-trade securities settled on a gross basis, and it is to be implemented within four months of issuance, per Business Today and LiveLaw.

Our view: this may reduce the margin locked up for investors who sell shares and then trade again in the cash segment, though the real effect will depend on how brokers and clearing corporations implement it. It also places more responsibility on trading members to check client margins. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: how do you expect the early pay-in margin waiver to change the way clients manage cash-segment positions around settlement?
